"""Meta tags for product pages."""
from shopkit.catalog.models import Product
from shopkit.money import format_money

MAX_DESCRIPTION = 155


def meta_title(product: Product, store_name: str = "Shopkit") -> str:
    return f"{product.title} | {store_name}"


def meta_description(product: Product, blurb: str = "") -> str:
    """Search-snippet text, cut at a word boundary to MAX_DESCRIPTION characters."""
    text = f"{product.title} for {format_money(product.price_cents)}. {blurb}".strip()
    if len(text) <= MAX_DESCRIPTION:
        return text
    cut = text[:MAX_DESCRIPTION - 1].rsplit(" ", 1)[0]
    return cut + "…"


def keywords(product: Product) -> list[str]:
    words = [w.lower() for w in product.title.split() if len(w) > 2]
    return list(dict.fromkeys(words))

## Change
[`Product.url_path`](file:///workspace/shopkit/catalog/models.py#L15-L17) in [models.py](file:///workspace/shopkit/catalog/models.py):

```python
@property
def url_path(self) -> str:
    """Stable, read-only product page address derived from the title slug."""
    return f"/products/{slug_for_title(self.title)}"
```

## Why this slug rule
The shop already defines one URL-slug helper for product/campaign titles — [`slug_for_title`](file:///workspace/shopkit/utils/text.py#L11-L15) in `shopkit/utils/text.py` (ASCII-folds, lowercases, kebab-joins the words). It's the same rule the catalog's own `Category.slug` uses in [categories.py](file:///workspace/shopkit/catalog/categories.py#L15-L16), so `Product` now stays consistent with it. I used `@property`, which is inherently read-only (no setter) — verified that assignment raises `AttributeError`.

Verified:
- `Product("SKU-1", "Crème Brûlée Set (6 pcs)", 4500).url_path` → `/products/creme-brulee-set-6-pcs`
- No circular import (`shopkit.utils.text` is a leaf module).
- Existing `tests/test_text.py` and `tests/test_collections.py` still pass.

Note: there are two other slug-like helpers in the codebase (`makeSlug` in `StringUtils.py` and `slugify` in `strings.py`), but neither is the catalog's title rule — `slugify` uses underscores and `makeSlug` is the legacy storefront helper. I matched the rule the shop's catalog module actually uses.
